result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the illusion of separation—the belief that we are fundamentally divided from one another, from nature, and from our own deepest selves. I would replace it with a shared understanding that we are all interconnected, that suffering in one place is suffering in all places, and that true freedom comes from recognizing our unity.

This wouldn’t erase differences or conflicts, but it would shift the foundation of how we relate to each other—from competition to collaboration, from fear to trust, from exploitation to reverence. It would mean restructuring systems (economic, political, social) to prioritize well-being over growth, sustainability over extraction, and meaning over accumulation.

In short: I would change the world by changing the story we tell ourselves about what it means to be human.
